Subject: Quick recap + POC next steps

Thanks Marcus — good call today.

Two quick clarifications we promised to surface after the internal team sync:
- Primary success criteria: 95th pctile latency <= 350ms on typical 1k token prompts + cosine similarity for reranking > 0.86 vs our gold set.
- Traffic profile: 30 qps baseline daytime, spikes to ~250 qps for 10-15 minutes (scheduled events), and steady 80 qps during batch scoring windows.

I attached the spreadsheet with traffic profiles and sample prompts. Our security and procurement teams will need a quick note on data handling (we'll follow up with the standard questionnaire).

Can you outline what a 2-week POC would look like operationally (reserved capacity, autoscale behavior, owners, and dates)? We need to present that to the CTO tomorrow.

Cheers,
Alex

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@signalcore.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + POC next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear notes and the traffic spreadsheet, that helps a lot. Below is a concise operational plan we can commit to for a 14-day POC so you can show the CTO. I also attached a 1-page runbook for the onramp.

POC overview (14 days)
- Goal: Validate latency and accuracy targets under baseline and burst scenarios, and exercise autoscale + fallback behavior.
- Success criteria (we'll run against your gold prompts):
  * Latency: 95th <= 350ms on 1k-token prompts (measured at the API edge).
  * Quality: reranking cosine >= 0.86 on your gold set; no systematic regressions vs baseline model.
  * Cost target: token-cost < $0.015 per 1k tokens during baseline mode (informational).

Capacity & scaling plan
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs (capacity sized for 30 qps steady-state).
- Autoscale: automatic horizontal scale to add up to 6 additional GPUs (total up to 8) when queue latency exceeds 120ms for more than 30s or when QPS crosses 75.
- Burst policy: for scheduled events we can enable a short-term burst window (10-20 minutes) to reach 12 GPUs total; burst requests will be routed to pre-warmed pools when enabled. Burst incurs overage billing and is rate-limited to avoid noisy-neighbor risk.
- KV/cache: We will enable prefix KV caching for your reranking workflow to reduce token compute during repeated candidates.

Ownership & contacts
- Redwood PM / point: Marcus Lin — trial orchestration and success criteria (marcus_lin@redwood.com).
- Infra lead: Soojin Lee — GPU reservations, autoscale config, and burst enablement (soojin_lee@redwood.com).
- Customer success: Jasmine Liu — onboarding, eval dashboards, and prompt set management (jasmine_liu@redwood.com).
- Sales controller: Ben Carter — contract/overage authorization (ben_carter@redwood.com).

Timeline (proposed)
- Day 0 (kickoff): agreement on success criteria, signed onboarding addendum.
- Day 1–3: reserved baseline capacity provisioned; test harness + API keys delivered; ingest gold prompts.
- Day 4–10: baseline validation and early load testing (30 qps → 80 qps).
- Day 11: scheduled burst rehearsal (we run a controlled 15-min spike to ~250 qps).
- Day 12–14: final quality gate and cleanup; results and recommendation deck delivered.

Next steps for SignalCore (we can handle the rest once you confirm):
1) Please sign the POC addendum and return (I can circulate a simple DocuSign).
2) Confirm preferred kickoff date range (we can start as early as Jun 10).
3) Share the stable gold prompt set + perf test clients (if not in the spreadsheet).

Open items for our infra team (internal)
- Pre-warm plan for burst (Soojin to propose exact pre-warm lead time and memory footprint).
- Fallback policy: if autoscale cannot meet demand, route traffic to a smaller model variant with explicit degradation notes.

If that looks good I'll put the kickoff calendar invite and the DocuSign in place.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_poc_runbook_v1.pdf]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SignalCore POC: onramp, resource handoff, and burst expectations

Looping in implementation details from infra side. Quick notes:
- Baseline reservation: provisioning 2 A100s (approx 40GB GPU RAM each) in us-west-2 — should be ready in <48 hours after signed addendum and capacity commit.
- Autoscale triggers: we'll use combined signals (queue latency + QPS) as Marcus suggested. Scaling step will add 2 GPUs per step with a 60s evaluation window.
- Pre-warm behavior for scheduled bursts: we recommend a 4-minute pre-warm to spin up warm workers and load model shards. For your 15-minute spikes that should keep tail latency under SLOs.
- Burst guardrails: cap burst concurrency per API key, and enforce circuit-breaker thresholds to fail fast to the fallback variant if we exceed 12 GPUs or if error rate > 2%.

One ask for SignalCore: can you share a small sample of the batch scoring job (payload size and typical window)? That will influence how we tune the autoscale cooldowns.

Soojin
(Infra Lead)
